notes:
VERDICT: DRIFT. Two of the preprod defects reproduce exactly on prod; one reproduces partially (key present, value differs from what preprod described); one does not reproduce at all.

PER-FIELD PREPROD vs PROD COMPARISON --
1. configuration_id (declared nullable integer, key absent): REPRODUCES. Confirmed absent as a key on all 4 sampled prod rows (TC-5508207 Failed, TC-5472086 Passed, TC-973763 Passed, TC-973754 Passed), same as all 14 preprod rows. Same behavior, both environments.
2. custom_fields (declared object, returns []): REPRODUCES. [] on all 4 prod rows, same as all 14 preprod rows. v1's schema is still uncorrected on this field even though v2's sibling entry was already fixed to declare an array -- this recheck confirms the v1 fix proposed in the preprod finding still applies on prod.
3. updated_by (undeclared key present): KEY PRESENCE REPRODUCES, VALUE DOES NOT. Present on all 4 prod rows (undeclared, as on preprod) but null on every one, versus preprod's description of a fully populated user object on all 14 of its rows. Most likely a data-state difference (preprod's fixture had been re-submitted/edited; these prod rows are pristine single-submission results) rather than a genuine environment-level serializer difference, but it was not possible to force an edit here (read-only probe) to confirm that theory directly. Recommend the index note this as 'present but only populated once a result has been edited after creation' rather than assuming it is always a full object.
4. info.truncated (undeclared key present on preprod): DOES NOT REPRODUCE on prod. All 4 prod info blocks came back as exactly {page, page_size, count, prev, next} -- no truncated key at all. This is a genuine environment difference worth flagging: either preprod's serializer adds a field prod's does not, or this is itself unstable/version-dependent. Since the declared info schema never required truncated in the first place, prod's behavior here actually matches the DECLARED contract more closely than preprod's did.
5. result_status full object (confirmed-good, not a drift): REPRODUCES. All 4 prod rows carry the complete object (id, field_value, internal_name, field_name, colour, value_category) exactly as declared and as seen on preprod -- v1 does not share v2's cut-down-to-field_value defect, on either environment. This independently corroborates, from the v1 side, what tests/live/runs/tm-prod/list_test_results_for_test_case.json already confirmed from the v2 side on these same TR-4827350 rows.

FIXTURE STALENESS (worth flagging for whoever maintains PROD-FIXTURE.md) -- TC-1041809/TR-3866741 (the Blocked example) and the alternate TR-1806940 Blocked candidate have both drifted since being recorded: TC-1041809 is no longer mapped into TR-3866741 at all (its case grid now shows 16 untested cases, none of them TC-1041809), and TR-1806940's case grid is now completely empty (0 cases) despite list_closed_test_runs still reporting a cached 1-Blocked/21-total and 1-Blocked/1-total respectively for these two runs. This is a pre-existing cached-aggregate-vs-live-grid discrepancy, out of scope for this capability, not investigated further. TR-1236825 (28 Passed cases) was used as a live, stable substitute and produced a consistent 4th and 5th data point.

ATTACHMENTS / STEP_RESULT / DATASET HUNT -- genuinely attempted, nothing populated found. Checked all 4 real results reachable in this probe (TR-4827350 x2, TR-1236825 x2) plus confirmed both Blocked candidates (TR-3866741, TR-1806940) no longer have any mapped/executed cases to check. attachments:[] and test_run_step_result:null on every row sampled; v1 has no dataset key at all (only v2 exposes dataset, and it too has never been seen populated across the whole campaign). Consistent with the rest of the campaign (preprod and prod, v1 and v2): these fields remain UNVERIFIED IN THEIR POPULATED FORM everywhere probed so far, including this recheck. Not claiming a populated shape that was not observed.

PAGINATION -- could not exercise p=2 anywhere: every call returned info.count:1 (or 0 for the stale row), matching len(test-results) exactly in every case, and next was always null. This capability is scoped to one case within one run, so at most one logged execution per call is structurally expected here -- same conclusion the v2 prod recheck reached. No case with more than one recorded attempt in the same run was found to exercise real paging.

No writes were made anywhere in this probe; only GET reads against project 332537, all within the designated read-only prod retest scope.
